name: ATGM Bunker
what: A low concrete bunker with a roof-mounted guided-missile launcher. Long range, slow reload, top-attack hits on armor.

name: SAM Site
what: Four-canister launcher on a pad. It reaches high-flying jets, which today only AA vehicles touch. It needs a Radar Station in range.
weak: Ground assault, EMP, strike jets that dive under radar

name: Laser CIWS
what: A pedestal laser that burns drones, rockets and mortar shells out of the air inside a short dome of cover.
weak: Tanks, artillery out of its range, smoke

name: Howitzer Pit
what: A dug-in 155-class gun behind a sandbag ring. Fixed position, very long range, and cheaper than a self-propelled gun.

name: Pop-up Remote Turret
what: A buried remote weapon station. It stays hidden from enemy fog until it fires, then pops up and drops back down.
strong: Infantry and light vehicles that walk into it

name: Pak Nest
what: A towed anti-tank gun dug in behind scrap plates and sandbags. Cheap, hard-hitting, easy to hide.

name: Flak Battery
what: A twin-barrel flak gun on a cross base. It fills the sky with bursts: area damage against every low flyer and drone in a cone.
weak: Jets above its ceiling, ground armor

name: Net Launcher Post
what: A scaffold tower that fires weighted nets. Each net catches one drone intact, and Human B can salvage it.

name: Mortar Pit
what: A sandbagged mortar pit with an ammo stack. Indirect fire over walls at short-to-medium range.

name: Pillbox
what: A hexagonal concrete pillbox with a riveted roof. A squad garrisons it and fires from the slits; it shows 6 garrison slots.

name: Arc Pylon
what: A coil pylon that chains lightning between nearby enemies. The more targets bunch up, the more it hurts.
weak: Artillery out of range, single heavy tanks

name: Pulse Spire Mk II
what: An upgraded Spire with a rotating emitter ring. It locks on to aircraft at long range and pulses them out of the sky.

name: Jammer Obelisk
what: A field generator. Enemy drones inside its rings lose their link and fall, and guided shots lose their lock.
strong: Drones, guided missiles, the Drone Team

name: Mass Driver
what: A rail-launched kinetic artillery platform with glowing capacitor banks. Very long range, slow cycle.
strong: Bases and static defenses at long range

name: Sentry Mine Turret
what: A buried hex disc that rises when enemies cross it and fires at close range, then re-buries. It can be painted in fields.

name: Sandbag Line
what: Infantry drag a line of sandbags anywhere. Units behind it get the cover bonus that today only hills give.

name: Trench Line
what: Dug zig-zag trench. Infantry in it take far less damage from small arms and shell splash, but move slowly.

name: Tank Traps
what: Steel hedgehogs and concrete dragon's teeth. They block vehicles completely, while infantry pass through.

name: Barbed Wire
what: Concertina coils on posts. Infantry crossing it slow to a crawl; flamers, engineers and tanks clear it.

name: Minefield
what: Painted as an area with a brush. Anti-tank and anti-personnel mines are hidden from enemies; the owner sees the dashed boundary.

name: Garrisonable Building
what: City blocks and ruins that squads can occupy. Sandbagged windows give cover, and garrison pips show how many squads are inside.

name: Camo Nets and Decoys
what: Nets hide a parked unit from recon until it moves. Inflatable decoy tanks and SAMs draw enemy strikes and artillery.

name: Nanite Wall
what: A Machine wall segment that slowly rebuilds its own breaches while it stays powered.

name: Phase Gate
what: Two emitter pylons with a shimmering field. Machine units pass through it and everything else is blocked; it replaces the Field Gate at Stage 9.

name: Tethered Recon Aerostat
what: A winch truck flies a tethered balloon with a sensor pod. It gives a huge sight radius over one area and is easy to shoot down.

name: Loitering Munition Truck
what: A truck with a six-cell launcher. Each cell launches a strike drone that circles until a target appears, then dives.

name: Drone Control Center
what: A building that boosts every friendly Drone Team in range: +1 charge, longer drone range and faster restock.

name: FPV Workshop
what: A corrugated shed where Human B solders FPV drones from scrap. It rebuilds Drone Team charges at base, and salvaged nets feed it.

name: Backpack Jammer Team
what: Two soldiers with backpack jammers and whip antennas. Enemy drones near them drift and crash; their own drones are not affected.

name: Scrap Shotgun AA Squad
what: Three troops with big-bore scrap shotguns that throw pellet clouds at anything flying low. Cheap counter-drone for the frontline.

name: Hive Node
what: A hexagonal hive that slowly spawns free micro-drones on its own and sends them to the nearest fight.

name: Swarm Queen
what: A large, slow hexacopter mothership that endlessly releases micro-drones while it lives. A priority target.

name: Mimic Drone
what: It reads as an enemy drone on the opponent's screen until it is within 3 tiles, then dives. It fools both AA targeting and players.

name: SP Howitzer
what: A tracked self-propelled gun with a big boxy turret. This is Human A's missing Stage 8 artillery: shoot, then relocate.

name: MLRS
what: A tracked rocket launcher with a 12-cell pod. It fires a ripple salvo over a wide area, then needs a long reload or a resupply.

name: Mine-Clearing Vehicle
what: A tank chassis with a front roller and a rocket line charge. It blasts a safe lane through a minefield and wire.
weak: AT guns, anything once it's alone

name: Bridge Layer
what: It unfolds a scissor bridge over a river or gap in a few seconds and can pick it back up. This opens crossings the map didn't plan for.

name: Command Vehicle
what: An 8-wheel armored command post with a mast and dish. It gives a mobile officer aura (morale, accuracy, call-ins) when parked.

name: Robotic UGV
what: A small remote tracked robot with a weapon station. Cheap and fearless; it doesn't count as infantry for wounded or morale.

name: Landship
what: Human B's super-heavy: a riveted land-cruiser with a main gun, two sponson guns and a smokestack. Slow and close to unkillable head-on.

name: Flak Halftrack
what: A halftrack with a quad flak mount in the bed. It escorts columns against helicopters and drones.

name: Armored Bulldozer
what: A heavy dozer with a slit-window armored cab. It builds walls and trenches under fire and shoves tank traps and wrecks aside.

name: Salvage Crane
what: A crane truck that hooks battlefield wrecks and hauls them to a Salvage Yard for resources, fitting Human B's salvage economy.

name: Motorcycle Scouts
what: Three motorcycles, one with a sidecar MG. Human B finally gets a recon role: fast, long sight, fragile.

name: Spider Mine Layer
what: A six-legged crawler that seeds Sentry Mines as it walks. It can lay a minefield behind a retreating army.

name: Hover Tank
what: A hovering battle tank that crosses water and beaches like land, so the Machine gets real amphibious armor.

name: Colossus Walker
what: The Machine's late-game centrepiece: a four-legged siege walker with a core cannon. A rifleman stands next to it for scale.

name: Assimilator
what: A crawler that claws wrecks apart and rebuilds them as Machine units. It is the Machine's answer to the B salvage economy.

name: Marines
what: Infantry trained for beach assault: they unload from landing craft faster and fight at full strength while wading.

name: Paratroopers
what: A squad that drops from a Transport Gunship or VTOL anywhere in sight and lands behind the lines.
weak: AA during the drop, quick-reaction forces

name: EOD Sappers
what: Two sappers who sweep an area, mark a safe lane, defuse mines and cut wire. This is the hard counter to minefields.

name: JTAC
what: A forward air controller with a laser designator and radio. Airstrikes and artillery called through them land faster and cost less.

name: MANPADS Team
what: A two-man team with a shoulder-fired heat-seeker that reaches helicopters and low jets. Fast to reposition.

name: Conscript Wave
what: Ten cheap, poorly armed conscripts in one purchase. They soak fire and capture ground fast, with low morale.

name: Satchel Sappers
what: Three sappers with satchel charges who sprint to a wall, gate or bunker and blow a breach.
weak: MGs, wire, anything that sees them coming

name: Marksman
what: Human B has no sniper. This is a cruder long-range rifleman who works best prone and picks off officers and crew.

name: Propaganda Team
what: A loudspeaker and banner team. It is a morale aura for friendly troops and a slow morale drain on enemies who hear it.

name: Shield Drone
what: A hovering drone that projects a curved energy shield in front of nearby Machine ground units, blocking small arms.

name: Stalker Synth
what: A tall synthetic hunter that cloaks while still and strikes officers and crews. It is the Machine's Special Forces equivalent.

name: Repair Swarm II
what: An upgraded Maintenance Swarm that repairs units in combat, not only buildings, and reconnects damaged Machine units.

name: Breacher Crawler
what: A cheap crawler with a shaped charge. It rushes a wall or gate and detonates, so the Machine finally gets a dedicated breacher.

name: Recon Plane
what: A rusty high-wing prop plane with a camera pod. It fills Human B's empty Stage 9 air slot: wide reveal sorties, no weapons.

name: AWACS
what: A large radar plane with a rotodome. It reveals all aircraft in a huge radius and sharpens friendly AA and SAM tracking.

name: Airlift Transport
what: A four-engine cargo plane for the "Airlift" order in vision image 01. It parachutes supply pallets or a light vehicle anywhere in sight.

name: Stealth Strike Drone
what: A flying-wing strike drone that radar can't see. AA only engages it once it fires or flies very close.
weak: Interceptors with AWACS, Pulse Spire Mk II

name: Supply Ship
what: A container-and-fuel ship that resupplies nearby vessels on Auto, the way logistics trucks do on land.

name: Fuel Tender
what: Human B's riveted tanker barge with round fuel tanks and a smokestack. It is the same resupply role as the A Supply Ship.

name: Charge Tender
what: A Machine catamaran with glowing battery cells. It recharges nearby Machine boats and hover units at sea.

name: Minesweeper
what: A small ship that trails a sweep cable and clears sea mines along its wake, opening lanes for landings.

name: Mine Barge
what: A rail-decked barge that drops contact mines behind it, sealing a channel or estuary.

name: Hovercraft
what: An air-cushion landing craft that carries one tank and crosses water, beach and flat ground without stopping to unload.
weak: Any armed boat, AT on the beach

name: AA Barge
what: A towed flat barge with three flak mounts. It gives Human B fleet air defence, since B has no AA ship today.

name: Lance Cruiser
what: The Machine's first warship: a sharp-hulled cruiser with a centreline rail lance for long-range shore and ship strikes.

name: Aircraft Carrier
what: G6 headline, already noted in PLAN_G5 D20. A floating airfield: the hangar system goes to sea, with jets launching and recovering on deck.
strong: Projects air power anywhere on water

name: Attack Submarine
what: G6 headline. Submerged boats are invisible without sonar (destroyers, frigates) and hunt ships and carriers.

name: Radar Station
what: It unlocks the SAM Site, warns of incoming aircraft on the minimap and extends AA lock range around it.

name: Forward Operating Base
what: A small walled compound near the front with a tent, a flag and a container HQ. It rebuilds and reinforces infantry, and supply trucks restock from it.

name: Vehicle Repair Bay
what: A garage with a gantry crane. Damaged vehicles parked inside repair fast and wrecks can be recovered into it.

name: Cruise Missile Battery
what: A late-game strike: an erector launcher raises one cruise missile that can hit any target in sight on a long cooldown.

name: Rail Yard
what: Lays rail tiles and builds armored trains. Rail lines move units and supply fast along a fixed route. This needs a new rail tile type.

name: Armored Train
what: A locomotive with a flak car and a gun car. It runs only on rails but carries heavy firepower and troops along them.
weak: Cut rails, bombers, AT at the rails

name: Scrapyard Crane
what: A gantry magnet crane over scrap piles. It is an upgrade to the Salvage Yard that turns hauled wrecks into steel faster.

name: Propaganda Tower
what: A lattice tower with loudspeakers and a banner. It is a base-wide morale buff and slows enemy capture of nearby territory.

name: Nanite Forge
what: A dome that releases a nanite cloud. Every Machine unit in a wide radius slowly self-repairs out of combat.

name: Overmind Uplink
what: An HQ add-on: a tall uplink that unlocks Stage 10 Machine tech and lets Coordinators command at any distance.
weak: Its own cost; a priority target

name: Relay Lattice
what: Small linked pylons that extend Machine power and build range along a chain, so the Machine can expand without full bases.
weak: Cutting one pylon breaks the chain

name: Stage 6: Rhomboid Landcrawler
what: Stage 6 "Industrial Revival" is unplayable today. Its signature piece is an early rhomboid tank with side sponsons, clumsy and terrifying.

name: Stage 10: Laser Tank
what: Stage 10 "Automated Technocracies". A sleek tank with a beam emitter: no ammo, but it draws power and overheats.

name: Stage 10: Exo-Suit Trooper
what: Heavy powered-armor infantry that walks through rifle fire, carries a rotary gun and counts as light vehicle armor.

name: 4th faction: Technical
what: An irregular faction's core unit: a pickup with a bed-mounted heavy gun, mismatched paint, fast and cheap.

name: 4th faction: Tunnel Network
what: Hidden tunnel entrances that move infantry between any two exits instantly, the irregulars' answer to transports.

name: 4th faction: Ambush Cell
what: A squad that hides in brush and ruins. It gets a first-strike damage bonus and is invisible until it opens fire.

name: 4th faction: Captured Tank
what: Irregulars repair and repaint enemy wrecks into their own units. Each one is a stolen tank with patchwork paint and a faction flag.
strong: Late-game punch for a poor faction
